data_flow.step: The planner decides to run generate-spec. On the first run `spec_file` is `None`. On a revision it is the path of the current spec, and `answers`, `changes`, `new_research_docs`, and `findings` hold only what the spec does not reflect yet. The spawn runs with `s.session_root` as its session dir.

The generate-spec prompt computes the run stamp once (a revision keeps the stamp already in the file name) and names the file `{session-dir}/ostra-spec-{run-stamp}-{topic-slug}.md`. On a revision the agent reads the spec file first, redoes only the affected steps, and sends an `update`.

The agent calls `Document` with `path`, and either `document` (first write) or `update`/`remove` (revision or parts). The native loop and the harness MCP bridge expose the same tool definition, whose `document` schema is `SpecDoc`.
Layer 1 policy runs `check_document` on the resolved `path` before the tool executes.
`execute` coerces any argument sent as JSON text into a value using the tool schema, then calls `doc::document`.

`document` maps the agent to `DocKind::Spec`, requires the file name to start with `ostra-spec-` and end in `.md`, and requires the parent dir to equal the execution's session dir (compared through `paths::fold`).

For `update`/`remove`, the stored JSON is loaded from `<stem>.json` and `apply_update` merges. A keyed list merges by id and sorts naturally. `remove` ids that match nothing fail the whole call before any write.

`doc::write` parses the merged value as `SpecDoc` (naming the failing field path on error), runs `check`, writes `<stem>.json` then `<stem>.md` in the same directory, and returns `Written` with the issues.

The tool marks both files as read for the agent and returns a summary: counts of criteria, deliverables, requirements, acceptance criteria, evidence rows, and open questions, the file paths, and the check issues. It tells the agent to fix errors with an `update` before submitting.

The agent calls `submit_generate_spec`. The tool boundary runs `check_submit`, which loads the JSON at `spec_path`, refuses on any error-level issue, and refuses when the submitted `external_evidence_rows`, `deliverables`, or `requirements` differ from the spec.

The fold records the result: `spec.current = Some(sub)`, `spec.applied = spec.sent`, `spec.version += 1`, pending findings cleared, approval revoked. The planner then asks open questions (Rule D3) before any fact-check, and a later revision reuses `spec.current.spec_path` as `spec_file`.
The console reads the file through the artifact endpoint, which returns the markdown content plus `load_view(&path)`, the typed document and its check results parsed from the stored JSON.

patterns.description: The spec is a session-level artifact. The generate-spec execution runs with the session root as its session dir (`ExecRecord` purposes Spec, Plan, and spec/plan fact-check use `session_root`; every other purpose uses `session_root/<project key>`). The session root is `<workspace>/.ostra/sessions/<session_id>`. So the spec lives at `<workspace>/.ostra/sessions/<session_id>/ostra-spec-{YYYYMMDD-HHmmss}-{topic-slug}.md`, with its source JSON at the same path with extension `.json` (`json_path` is `md.with_extension("json")`). Both files sit directly in that directory: the tool rejects a path in a subdirectory. Research documents, by contrast, sit in the per-project subdir `<session root>/<project key>/ostra-research-*.md` plus `.json`. A plan adds `ostra-plan-*-phase-{N}.md` and `.json` pairs beside the master. The engine does not store the spec content in its event log: the `GenerateSpecSubmit` payload (with `spec_path`, counts, summary, open questions) goes into the log and `SessionState.spec.current`, and the file content stays on disk. The engine-owned `.state` dir in the session root is separate and no agent may write there. The fact-check agent copies only the `.md` into `factcheck-snapshot-spec/` in the session dir, which is why a revision must keep the file name.
patterns.name: Storage layout of the spec

patterns.description: `store::write` parses and checks the value first. Only if parsing succeeds does it write `<stem>.json` (pretty-printed with a trailing newline) and then `<stem>.md` (rendered). A schema failure writes nothing. Check errors do not block the write; they are returned to the agent and block the later submit. A plan additionally writes `-phase-{N}` pairs and deletes stale phase files; the spec writes one pair only.
patterns.name: JSON is the source, markdown is rendered

patterns.description: `apply_update` replaces each top-level field named in `update`. When both the stored value and the new value are arrays and every item has an `id` (string or number), items merge by id: a known id replaces the stored item whole (shallow, not a field-level merge inside the item), a new id is appended, and the list is re-sorted in natural id order (`R2` before `R10`). Any other field, including an array without ids such as `notes`, is replaced. `remove` then drops items by id from every keyed list in the document, and fails with `Nothing to remove for ...` and no write if an id matches nothing. The generate-spec prompt states the same rule: a known id replaces the stored entry whole, and a changed requirement is sent whole with all its acceptance criteria. Note: the Document tool description shown to some agent runs says a merged item 'keeps the rest, at every level'; the repo's `DOCUMENT` constant in defs.rs:101 and `apply_update` do not do that, so the code is authoritative here.
patterns.name: Keyed-list merge for revisions

patterns.description: The tool accepts exactly one of two shapes. `document` alone writes the whole document and replaces what is stored. `update` and/or `remove` without `document` load the stored JSON (`doc::load(&md)`), apply the merge, and write the result through the same `doc::write`. `document` together with `update` or `remove` is an error. `remove` with no stored document is an error. The merged value is validated as a whole, so a revision that leaves the spec invalid is rejected and nothing is written. Arguments sent as JSON text are coerced to values against the tool schema in `execute` before this runs.
patterns.name: Document tool input resolution

patterns.description: The write guard (Layer 1) refuses Write, Edit, and shell writes to any file in the session dir whose name starts with `ostra-research-`, `ostra-spec-`, or `ostra-plan-` and ends in `.md` or `.json`, with the correction to use `Document`. Snapshot copies under `factcheck-snapshot-*` are exempt. The Document tool call itself is checked by `check_document`: the target must match the agent's owned artifact pattern, and with tool enforcement it must lie inside the execution's session dir.
patterns.name: Documents change only through the Document tool

document.problem: The spec is a typed document (`SpecDoc`) that the generate-spec agent writes through one tool, `Document`. Ostra stores the JSON as the source and renders the markdown from it. A revision must edit the same file in place and send only what changed. This document records exactly how each of those steps works in the code today, because the spec and plan stages depend on the file name, the merge semantics, and the JSON/markdown pairing.

It does not cover the fact-check agent's internals, the research and plan documents beyond where they share code, or the web UI rendering of a document.

submit.findings_summary: The spec is a typed SpecDoc. The Document tool (crates/ostra-tools/src/doc.rs) validates the name (`ostra-spec-{stamp}-{slug}.md`, directly in the session dir) and calls `doc::write`. That writes `<stem>.json` as the source and renders `<stem>.md` beside it. Both live in the session root `<workspace>/.ostra/sessions/<session_id>/`. A revision sends `update`/`remove` against the stored JSON; `apply_update` merges keyed lists by id with whole-item replacement (not a field-level merge) and sorts them naturally. The planner passes `spec_file` on a rerun so the agent edits the same path, and the fold increments `spec.version`. Layer 1 guards deny direct writes to these files, and `check_submit` refuses a submit when the stored spec has errors or its counts disagree.

data_flow.step: An agent calls the `Document` tool; `store::write` validates the value with `DocKind::parse`, runs `check`, writes `<name>.json` (pretty JSON of the submitted value) and renders `<name>.md`. A plan also writes `-phase-N` json and md pairs and deletes stale phase files.
The user opens a file. The tab resource is `artifact:<absolute md path>` (or route `/w/:ws/artifact?path=`). `screens/index.tsx` renders `ArtifactScreen` for resource type `artifact`.
`ArtifactScreen` calls `api.artifact(path)` through `useAsync(..., [path])`. `api` is `httpApi` unless `VITE_MOCK=1`.

`httpApi.artifact` issues `GET /api/artifacts?path=<encoded>` via `request`, with same-origin cookies. A 401 fires the `onUnauthorized` listeners; other non-2xx responses throw `HttpError(status, error, issues)`.
The server middleware `guard` checks Host, Origin, and the cookie for everything under `/api/`.
Route `/api/artifacts` calls `artifact`. `session_file` canonicalizes the path, requires it to sit inside some workspace's sessions root (403 otherwise, 404 if missing, 400 if not a file).

If the file is at most 4 MiB and reads as UTF-8, the handler computes `headings` and calls `ostra_core::doc::load_view(&path)`. Otherwise it returns `binary: true` with empty content and `document: None`.

`load_view` maps the file name prefix to a `DocKind`, reads `json_path(md)`, parses it (`PhaseDoc` for phase files, `DocKind::parse` otherwise), runs `check`, and returns `DocumentView { document, issues }`; any failure returns `None`.

Back in `ArtifactScreen`, `typed = art.data?.document`. It looks up the owning session in the live workspace tree, fetches `api.session(owner.id)`, and `pickFactCheck(detail.data?.fact_checks, target)` selects the spec or plan fact-check (research and no-owner documents get none).

When `typed` is present and the Markdown toggle is off, `ArtifactScreen` renders `DocumentView` with the toolbar/title/EARS note as `header`. Otherwise it renders the markdown outline and `ArtifactMarkdown` from `art.data.content` and `headings`.

`DocumentView` builds marks from `view.issues` and the fact-check (`buildMarks`), builds chapters with `outlineOf`/`docChapters`, picks the current chapter from the URL hash (`parseAnchor`), and renders the menu, issue banner (Overview only), the chapter's `render()`, and the pager. Navigation calls `nav.open('artifact:<path>', { anchor })`, so chapter and element are stored in the URL hash.

The server reads that file as text for `content` and `headings`, then calls `load_view(&path)`, which derives the kind from the file name prefix (`ostra-research-`, `ostra-spec-`, `ostra-plan-`), reads the `.json` sibling, parses it, and runs `check`. The web imports them from `web/src/api/gen/` through `web/src/api/types.ts` re-exports. Per CLAUDE.md, run `cargo test -p ostra-core` after a Rust type change, then `cd web && npm run typecheck`.

document.problem: Typed documents are stored as JSON beside a rendered markdown file. The console never requests the JSON directly: it requests the markdown file by path and receives the parsed document inside the same response. This document records that path so a change to document shape, versioning, or fetching starts from the real code.
document.scope: Task: how the console shows a typed document (research, spec, plan, phase) and fetches it from the API. Covers the server read path, the DTOs, the web fetch and render path, and the mobile reuse. It does not cover how agents write documents (the Document tool), the fact-check pipeline, or the markdown renderer.
document.title: Console display and fetch of a typed document

submit.findings_summary: The console fetches a typed document through GET /api/artifacts?path=<md path>. The handler returns Artifact, whose document field is a DocumentView (document plus issues) built by ostra_core::doc::load_view from the .json sibling of the rendered markdown. ArtifactScreen calls it once per path with useAsync, and gets fact-checks from the owning session's detail. DocumentView turns the Document enum (research, spec, plan, phase) into paged chapters through per-kind outline builders, with marks from issues and fact-check findings and #chapter/element deep links. When document is null or the user toggles Markdown, the screen falls back to the markdown view. The mobile screen reuses docChapters.
